text_fidelity_a:
Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans So far, I am underwhelmed. I purchased this in advance of a cross-country trip and an extended stay in a budget hotel that doesn't have a room fridge - hence the choice of dual power source. Being the prudent sort, I plugged it in at home to see whether it really would cool down to 40 degrees. House was 75 degrees, cooler after running all night was 55 degrees, at best. I'll probably keep it, and maybe as a beer or cola cooler it's fine, but as for being able to keep perishables such as eggs, milk, lunch meat and cheese in the hotel, or in transit for 1000 miles, for that matter, I'm not sure it's worth the risk of food poisoning to rely on its cooling capability. It's also smaller inside than I was expecting.

Update: On a second, and much longer, trip, I took this along, mostly for refrigeration in transit, but then when I reached my destination, I found that the full-size fridge was on the blink, so I plugged this in and it kept stuff reasonably cold, including the return trip, although still not much lower than 40-degrees. All told, some of the stuff I carried with me was still good when I got back home eleven days later, and maybe some of that was due to having also packed big bottles of frozen drinking water (ice) and starting out with other frozen foods; maybe some of it was due to my travel being in weather that was at freezing or below and the cooler rode for part of the trip in an unheated truck boot. All that being said, I still wouldn't be totally reliant on it in the summer, and would still pack the bottled ice - which is also a good way to gauge just how well the cooler is doing its job.
text_fidelity_b: Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans

text_fidelity_a: 13 Fishing - Kalon A - Spinning Reels We have been waiting for the chance to review these 13 Fishing Kalon reels.  We finally got the chance this past weekend to get out and test the 4.0, the 2.0 and then this 0.5 right here.  Of the three, this one is about as standard as they come.  Nothing fancy about this one, and there were several things that made me feel like this reel would actually be the most effective starter reel for kids.  By saying that, I don't mean to imply that it looks like a kids toy reel, I just mean in the way that the construction is done to where you don't have anything to really worry about getting all scratched up, plus the plastic handle has more of a rubber grip for non-slip, little wet hands.  I found that quite nice so that was one of my first thoughts.  We had our 11 year old start out with this reel, and he has had his fair share of fishing excursions so he is not entirely a new angler, and he immediately reported that he love how light the feel was, the crank was smooth, that the retrieve was smooth, and that he didn't have some of the reel tangle or hitching that he has with his other reel.  Not entirely sure how long this will hold up only time will tell of course as with any other reel.  For a more affordable reel, this seems like it is going to do well for him.  Fishing gear has become quite costly, as with everything else these days, and I feel like this reel for our purpose, still falls in line with the other 2 Kalon reels we have tested out this weekend, just as budget friendly and would also make a nice gift.  Your more professional anglers probably would pass on this reel, and that's perfectly okay.  Construction of a reel is pretty important, but also, aesthetics tend to play a part even if they try to tell you it doesn't.  So if I were to have anything objective to add to this review, it would only be that it looks a little on the cheap side, but I can say, I tried it out too and it does not perform cheaply.  I do recommend this reel especially for beginners and I hope you find this review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: 13 Fishing - Kalon A - Spinning Reels

I would have sworn I was getting more sleep and sleeping like a log.  Flex tells me the brutal truth that I am way below the amount of sleep I need and am way more restless during the little sleep I do get.  I am trying slowly, but surely, to increase the amount of sleep I get.  I have a bit of frustration while gardening because some of my activities create enough vibration to cause the device to think I'm going to sleep.  I've worn it in the shower from the beginning and everything still works well.  In fact, the only time I've removed it except for recharging was for a formal event (and only because I could not find a bracelet that would camouflage it well enough!!).  I would recommend this device.  It gives you a reality check and could motivate you to make some adjustments for a healthier lifestyle.  It gets 4 stars instead of 5 simply because it can't tell when I'm gardening.  :-)

text_fidelity_a:
Lifetime 48 Quart High Performance Hard Cooler First, the good: Man, does this thing keep cold. I wanted to test it before I decided to keep it so pre-chilled it with 8 pounds of cold packs, about 5 pounds of 32F (AKA water) freeze point and about 3 pounds of 28F freeze point gel packs. I let this pre-chill the cooler for about 4 hours which lowered the temp down to 40F. I then placed my test ice - 1 quart of water at about 0F - into the cooler. The test ice remained frozen for 2 1/2 days. At the end of the test all of the 32F cooling blocks had thawed but the 28F blocks still had some ice left in them. So, yeah, with some more high-tech ice and filled with more than a quart block of ice this cooler will keep things cold for a long time.

Now, the bad: Come on Lifetime, you make like Made in the USA is a big deal and then you allow seams like the attached photos past quality control. Finish matters. This was a surprise (particularly the open seam) as the rest of cooler seemed really well constructed. I'm not sure if that open seam would allow water into the insulation area but I'm going to slap some sealant on it to be sure it won't. I'll get rid of those rough spots, too.

Otherwise it's a really good cooler, it would have been a solid 5-stars if only it was as well made as the Chinese products.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime 48 Quart High Performance Hard Cooler

All the sudden it would still charge fine but a full charge that initially would last almost a week, was now barely giving me 24 hours of usage of the flex.
I contacted customer support and the only way to do so is using email. It takes them about 2 days to get back to you (had issues before and it took that time both times). They told me the firmware needed to be upgraded and would improve the performance of the flex. I did that and sure enough no change. The full charge still drains within a day and makes the unit rather useless. Having a week on one charge wasn't too great to begin with but having to charge it every day?

I informed customer support that it was still not working, well that was a few days ago and I still haven't heard a thing back from them about replacing or fixing it.

Rather disappointed in the customer service. You can't find a phone number to actually just call and get things done and the support with email takes days to even get a reply.

I was going to get the new unit they have the force, but now considering their customer support I might just cut my losses.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

text_fidelity_a:
[New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack The rack is solid. Really easy to attach to the hitch. In our case I have to problem whatsoever to attach it when we need it and remove it right after use using the included hardware. One review mentioned that leaves it exposed to a theft, so I tossed a wrench and remove the rack while we are biking (it takes about a minute). Perhaps the greatest feature are those bike cradles and straps. We transport 3 bikes - 1 men frame, 1 women and 1 children's. They all hang at different angles, but all 3 are very solid and unmovable. The collapsible frame is a nice feature too. Once I forgot to close the door while I already had one bike attached to the rack (yeah, I was tired after a long ride :-)) Lowered the rack with that bike on it, closed the door, return the rack back to upright position and kept loading the remaining 2 bikes.

The only (perceived maybe) con of this rack - it is a bit wobbly when it is loaded and the car is moving. When I keep that in mind and drive a bit more carefully that does not appear to be an issue. Note that bikes are attached securely and do not move at all even a little bit relative to each other or to the frame. But the entire thing wobbles slightly left and right when the car moves on an uneven pavement. I do not think this is a hitch connector issue as it fits snugly into a hitch receiver. Could be that the 1.25" to 2" adapter just cannot provide enough support. Or maybe that's the inherent weakness of hitch-mounted racks (the connection to the receiver cannot be rigid enough). Or both... Take into account that this is our first rack and I have no experience whatsoever with other racks. They probably all wobble, I just do not have a good reference to say whether this wobbles more or less.
text_fidelity_b: [New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack

Synergee Exercise Fitness Resistance Band Mini Loop Bands That Perform Better When Working Out at Home or The Gym [[VIDEOID:50a12e8589c908f169d5d2cabe52ea8d]] i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. i was not influenced by anyone in any way.

Strength Bands are an incredible versatile tool for adding resistance to stretching, lifting, and body weight training exercises. There are a lot different workouts you can do with these bands. I have larger and longer ones that I have used for conditioning as well as therapy. They increase your flexibility and strength. These mini bands, each one gives a different level of resistance. I have not tried the mini bands, so I was anxious to try these out. I love the way they feel and have researched some good workouts to do. I wish I had gotten some of these mini bands a long time ago.

YELLOW: the most common color for bands that provide very light resistance, very little tension, which mean that they are stretchy, and take little effort to pull against them and stretch them out. Yellow is used for rehabilitation purposes and to work small, stabilizing muscles, such as the rotator cuff muscles in the shoulder joints. I use this color a lot because of my ripped rotary cuffs. They help to keep my arms conditioned but not in pain.

GREEN: Green resistance bands are medium resistance. These bands are less stretchy and have more tension than yellow bands. Green bands are used for muscle groups that need slightly more tension, such as the biceps or triceps. Good choice for pull up training. Resistance is 50 – 120 pounds.

BLUE: are heavy resistance. Blue bands are for those who are very strong, or for those larger muscle groups, such as the legs, chest and back. Also a good choice for adding increment weight to power lifts. Resistance 60 – 150 pounds.

BLACK: have the most resistance. These are the hardest bands to stretch and pull. Like blue bands, black bands are used for the large muscle groups, such as the legs, or when working with others. Some sets of bands come in all black and the level of resistance is not based on color in these sets. For power lifts. Resistance is 80 to 200 pounds

The wider the band is, the more resistance it offers. You should choose the appropriate tension based on your current fitness level and exercise goals. One person may use a heavy band to do sets of eight-repetition chest presses, another person may only use a medium band. As with any form of resistance, start light and gradually increase the resistance over time.

text_fidelity_a:
BalanceFrom Vertical Climber with Cast Iron Frame and Digital Display [Newest Version] I'm 5'3", and I used to use the VersaClimber at the gym years ago. I'm involved in rehabbing my legs from injury, and thought if I used this very slowly just a few steps a day to start with, it could be useful. And for the price, this is an unbeatable value, so I decided to give it a shot.

My handy husband built the climber in about 15 minutes, and it was sturdier than expected. As others say, the instructions are useless, but it did come with extra hardware that we didn't need. Once it was built, he gave it a try. He's 6' 7" and found the geometry didn't work for him. It wasn't as loud as some people describe and the action was smoother than we expected. Then I tried it.

As mentioned, I'm 5' 3" with a 27 to 28" inseam. Once you put your first foot on a pedal, you press down, and the pedal with no foot on it goes to the top of its travel; at that point I was literally unable to reach the second pedal. I have a full range of motion - I'm just not very tall. I actually tried to use a stool to get my second foot on the second pedal, but it was pretty precarious. If you're my height with very strong arms to keep the unmanned pedal from going all the way up, this could be a handy machine. if you're taller than I, it could be a great alternative to a stepper.

There is a 17.5 inch distance between pedals when one is at the top of its travel and the other is at its bottom. If your legs are strong enough, you could probably keep each stroke from going to the top or the bottom.

Btw, while the manufacturer claims this climber has a cast iron frame, of course it doesn't, and since cast iron is porous, it's just as well.

It's better quality machine than I expected, and steadier on a hardwood floor than I expected, too. Just not right for me. But if you need a climber, it's a good value and probably as good in quality as the ones costing twice as much or more.
text_fidelity_b: BalanceFrom Vertical Climber with Cast Iron Frame and Digital Display [Newest Version]

text_fidelity_a:
IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine Let me start by saying I have been lifting in gyms for about 30 years and even qualified for Nationals as bodybuilder when I was 27....I'm 43 now. Still going at it strong but wanted a home calf raise machine and an alternative to barbell squats. I've probably lifted on just about any and all commercial grade equipment out there. Here are my thoughts on this piece of equipment and why I only gave it 3 stars. I hope it helps.

1) As others have stated...there are no directions and let's be serious...how irritating is that? If you can't bother giving your customer assembly instructions how much can you really honestly care about your customer? Just my two cents.

2) The contents are ill packaged and yes, I understand that Fed Ex shakes the boxes. But both boxes looked like they were packaged by a 5 year old. Just a total mess...screws...bolts...washer...thrown around in the box with shredded styrofoam and broken tight downs. I can't possibly see how any shipper could have created this total mess. Again, extreme sloppiness leads me to believe there is a lack of concern for the person receiving it.

3) 50% of the reason I purchased this piece of equipment was for the standing calf raise, my local gym only has the seated calf raise. I've had this exact same piece of equipment before by PowerTec....and I wasn't sure how I was going to feel about the rounded calf raise platform versus the flat one that power tec made and every other commercial grade piece of gym equipment uses. Now I know why they don't use a rounded platform. U have less contact material with your foot when you raise up. Is it the end of the world? No...but I'm just not a huge fan of the rounded platform. I much more prefer the standard flat platform that feels natural and more comfortable on the feet.

4) The step up from floor level to the calf raise machine is a bit hairy once you get some heavy weight on the machine...3 to 4...45's on each side. I wish the platform was designed differently so all that weight is not stacked onto on leg and your back is torqued when you step up. Commercial grade equipment is made in such a way that the platform is directly under you....you start on the calf platform...you don't load the weight and then step up. This machine is set up so that in order to have the weight directly on your shoulders...where it needs to be....you are standing one step behind the calf platform. Then in order to do the calf raise...you have to step up onto the platform...one leg at at time with all the weight on your back and one leg down...and one leg taking a step. Not good in my opinion.

5) The angle of the squat. Ahh...its okay....makes you feel like you are doing a deep squat but in reality even a deep squat on this machine is not even a parallel squat. If you have someone else do a deep squat and watch their lower leg in relation to their upper...you will see that the deepest squat on this machine is still a high squat in reality. Your leg is simply at a different angle and gives the false sense that you are performing a deep squat...when in fact you are not.

Will this take the place of a regular squat?

Yes, and No.

If you are a gym rat and you perform squats correctly than this piece of equipment will never take the place of or produce the same results.

If you are like 95% of the guys in the gym that never ever reach parallel when they squat because they were too busy stacking on the weight instead of learning good form at the beginning...than yes...this piece of equipment will keep you squatting a bit high and allow you to keep stacking the weight on and the ego flying high.

Can you get a good calf workout on this machine?

Absolutely. Even with the rounded platform that I do not like...you can still get a great calf workout.

Would I buy it again?

I'm on the fence with this one. I wouldn't cry if it was removed from my home...but I wouldn't send it back either.

I use the squat portion in addition to my leg workout....not as my primary piece of equipment...and I think that is what it is good for...and addition to regular squats....leg press...lungs...extensions...curls...etc. etc.

Hope my review helped somone.
text_fidelity_b: IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine

ust Heritage Lensatic Compass with Lightweight Brass Construction for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Hunting and Outdoor Survival This UST HERITAGE LENSATIC COMPASS is beautiful, with its liquid-filled needle capsule, and its polished brass case. It’s fairly heavy (4.7 oz.), so it may not be the best choice for backpacking, but it’s a great learning compass.

To use it, the first step is to hold it level, so that the needle swings freely without touching the sides of the capsule. The second step is to make sure there is no metal (e.g., a hunting knife) or magnetic field nearby, as either will affect the needle direction and prevent an accurate reading. The third step is to let the needle “settle” before you take your reading.

The box says there are complete instructions for use inside—NOT true, but the Ultimate Survival Technologies web site has an excellent one-page PDF that gives two methods for using the compass to sight distant objects and determine directions. “Lensatic” means that the compass has a prismatic lens for reading the outer (mils/milliradians) or inner (degrees) scales and determining the bearing or azimuth. This lens really works—it magnifies the scale figures.

The luminous directional letters and sighting lines also work. The “hanging loop” is actually a thumb loop that helps you steady the compass as you sight with it. My brass case has a few tiny nicks and pits on the bottom and on the lens pivot, but the brass cover is pristine and gorgeous. I polish the case with Brasso.

Once you have this compass, you can learn all about navigation. Start by looking up “Compass” on Wikipedia, and it will lead you to many fascinating online articles.
text_fidelity_b: ust Heritage Lensatic Compass with Lightweight Brass Construction for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Hunting and Outdoor Survival

text_fidelity_a:
Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag We bought this flag to hang outside of our house on game day. I scoured Amazon for a couple of hours (at least) trying to find the best flag with the best value. I read a lot of reviews on a similar flag, in which most people said the flag was very thin. In my mind, thin does not equal quality, so I was highly drawn towards this flag because it's embroidered. Even though it was double the price, I figured the embroidery was worth it.

We received the flag in the mail pretty quickly, but immediately from its opening, the flag was bleeding color. :( Not sure if it was the thread they used in the embroidery, or the flag itself, but the white part of the Seahawks logo had significant purple coloring on it that looked like it was coming from the edges/embroidery. SUCH A BUMMER. We tried to see if we could wash it off, but it wouldn't come off, so naturally, we returned it. We live in Hawaiʻi where the weather is unpredictable and rains off and on a lot... so we didn't want more bleeding to occur while we hung it outside.

The flag was thick and felt like a durable and good quality material, but the bleeding was obviously a make or break for us. We ended up purchasing the "thin" flag that was half the price of this one and that one is perfect (despite being thin). Not sure if we just got a dud, or what, but based off of our experience, I wouldn't order this again.
text_fidelity_b: Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag

This mess kit is also very easy to clean and the paint doesn't flake off even in high heat. i couldn't believe I got one of this kits for a bargain price but has apart of History in it. Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can Some Augason Farms stuff I buy as emergency food, some I buy for regular use. If I can price out something in this form that is same price or less than other forms, then I go with this as it can be stored away or kept in my working pantry. I use a lot of Augason Farms, and I've been pleased with this.

Dehydrated celery is a great addition to the pantry. Sometimes I dont have fresh, or I have fresh that went bad, or I dont find it in the store, or what is there looks bad, or price is way outside my budget. Having some dried celery tucked away in my pantry really helps stretch the budget and brings value to my time.

I keep the recipe trifecta on hand, "mire poix": celery, carrot, and onion. I keep fresh, frozen, and dried on hand. Usually used in recipes that will help rehydrate these foods no problem. Celery is very easy to rehydrate. I usually just add to the cooking process and its good to go.

Food scarcity is legit, so if you can stock up when items are on sale, then I recommend to do so. Consider it insurance.

FYI: food and such are sold based on weight, not volume. There is 1lb, 2 oz packed in this #10 can (that reads, "number ten" not "ten pound"- it is a size of can). Using a #10 can means that it provides uniformity among storage. Emergency supplies are packed for long term and are packed to stack. They also float. They can be repurposed. Even if one gets a dent, contents are still good (unless and actual hole, which is not likely to happen). The food will not be filled to the brim, and also.. food settles after packing.

text_fidelity_a:
Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal) --Preamble--

Like many people, I decided to try out some thick bar grips to optimize my current regimen. I too was attracted by the idea of improving my grip and strengthening the whole complex of muscles/tendons/ligaments in my forearms. So I purchased four kinds of wide bar grips - Fat Gripz One (1.75"), Fat Gripz Pro (2.25"), Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips (2"), and Yes4All Thick Bar Grips (2.2").

Before the review, some context:

First, you should ease into these things, and so if you aren't accustomed to thick bar grips, I would recommend you start with the Fat Gripz One. I did not do this; I tried to integrate all four into my routine, and as a result I gave myself acute tendonitis in both arms, in the form of Golfer's Elbow. Now I need to take at least 4 weeks off while I heal up, and no one likes that. I don't think this would have been a problem if I just started with the narrower grips and moved up from there.

Second, if use a ruler, my hand is 6 5/8" (168mm) from the bend of the wrist to the tip of my middle finger. The Fat Grips One is fine, the Iron Bull Strength grips are about the limit of decent grip, and the Fat Grips Pro are too large to get my hand around, limiting me to fairly light dumbbells. For pull-ups, only the Fat Grips one are comfortable, the Iron Bull's are marginal. I have chronic issues with my TFCC (something I was hoping to help alleviate through these grips) and the thicker ones tend to aggravate that complex.

Lastly, I am fairly fit. I am about 183lbs (83.2kg) and was doing sets of 23 pull-ups before this. I could maintain those numbers with the narrower wide grips, but with greater effort. I have my pull-up bar (an Iron Gym) wrapped in racket grip tape, so it is about 1.1" in diameter. Most of my dumbbells have bars that are between 1.1 and 1.25" in diameter.

--Product Review--

The Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 are a respectable alternative to the Fat Gripz. They have a different profile, being more curved in the center, which I don't necessarily prefer, but it isn't really a negative, just different. They are firmer than Fat Gripz, but not much less grippy. I prefer how they look, being all black, no colored logos to distract the eye. As for the scent, they smell like coconut oil to me, which is pleasant.

---Comfort

The Iron Bull Alpha Grips are fairly comfortable, not as much as the Fat Gripz Pro but close. Like other thick bar grips they have a raised pattern pressed into the rubber which give more of an inconsistent surface than an uncomfortable one. The suitability of the raised bump in the middle is going to be highly subjective; I personally like it on dumbbells, but not on my pull-up bar. These have a seam, just like all thick bar grips, though it is smaller than some cheaper models. These don't fit on IronMaster dumbbells due to them having a 1.25" bar, but they fit CAP models and my pull-up bar, an Iron Gym, pretty well. I find the 2" diameter is much nicer to work with than the 2.25" of the Fat Gripz Pro.

---Benefit

Decent benefit, it has an immediately noticeable visual effect, within a week anyway. I had to drop 20% of my reps to compensate, but before the injury I could feel the improvements already, such that it felt odd not to use them. Whereas before the IronMaster bar felt thick, now it feels fairly thin. Definitely helps improve general muscle tone and forearm strength and feels, at least, like the exercises are more engaging. Effect is as described, and I imagine one would see real benefits in muscle mass within a month.

---Conclusion

I'd recommend these as a solid alternative to the Fat Gripz, not necessarily better or worse, but merely different. Presently, I like the Fat Gripz One for pull-ups, the Fat Gripz Pro for light weights (<30lb), and the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 for medium weights (30lb-55lb).
text_fidelity_b: Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal)

Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack, Model ZN102, Black This is a good bicycle carrier, though could be improved. This was used to transport two “adult” and one “women's” bicycles for a 2000 mile move on the back of a Kia Forte 5 Door hatchback. The bicycles were secured with bungee cords to keep the handle bars from moving.

Some reviewers pointed out that it's difficult to put three bicycles on this rack, I didn't have this issue because in my case one of the bikes had a different geometry from the other two. If you have three bicycles with identical geometry this might be an issue though.

Don't underestimate how tight the straps need to be. On the Kia Forte 5 door there is no way to attach the bottom straps to the bumper cover. I had to attach both of the bottom straps to the tow hook on the metal frame of the bumper on the driver side. After the first 500 miles, one of the bottom straps loosed up which made the rack rock side to side which caused the passenger side lateral strap to slide down and scratch the paint. After I put in some effort in re-tightening the straps the rack stayed in place for the next 1500 miles. While I suspect that if the straps are tight the car paint will be safe, I do wish that the hooks had some kind of soft rubber coating.

Except for the paint scratch from the strap hook, the rack fared well.

text_fidelity_a:
Skechers Women's GO Walk High Waisted Legging As a Lululemon aficionado, I'm frequently disappointed by the pants offerings from other companies. But where Lululemon falls short is that they rarely put pockets on their high waisted pants, leaving me trying to find weird solutions to keep my cell phone on me, such as a cell phone pocket scarf, a cell phone lanyard that is worn around the neck, armbands, etc. I don't want all of that business, I just want to put my phone in my pocket. I have to keep it on me constantly for work, so it's important to me.

So I was absolutely delighted to see that skechers has come out with this offering of awesome, high waisted pants that actually stay put and do not slip down, that have two generously sized pockets! The material is medium thick and completely not see-through, like the old-school Lululemon fabric used to be, hides any number of lumps and bumps, is just compressive enough to feel flattering and comfortable yet not so compressive that I feel sweaty and eager to take the pants off. The high waist has a normal larger waistband like most types of yoga pants with this cut, but then they also have an additional elastic band that runs right around the top, which really holds the pants in place. It does cause a little bit of a belly roll where it sits, but usually my shirt hides it and it's worth it to not have to pull my pants up constantly throughout the day, especially when they are holding up my heavy cell phone as well.

I am usually a size 8 in Lululemon pants, which puts me right between a size medium and a size large in this brand. I feel like the medium is just a little too tight, and the large has a little extra fabric around the crotch. I settled on the medium for actually working out, and the large for lounging around the house, since I would usually lounge with a long tunic top any way and would prefer to be comfortable. I wish that they came in numbered sizing rather than small medium large sizing, so that there would be more size options in between medium and large.

However, if a person is lucky enough to fit squarely into one of the sizes, I think these pants would make most women happy. When they first arrived, they looked slightly short and cropped, but they actually fit me like full-sized pants, I think they stretch lengthwise once you put them on.
text_fidelity_b: Skechers Women's GO Walk High Waisted Legging

text_fidelity_a: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras The first trail cam we ever purchased, while we were not trying to be cheap about it, because of our lack of experience at the time with trail cams, we also didn't want to spend a ton but the first one we had was around $129 and it was absolutely a joke.  The night vision on that cam couldn't have possibly been worse, unless it just didn't work at all, but it worked slightly, however definitely not good enough for $129.  The picture quality was that of a child's first camera, to say the least.  So we decided to give this Dsoon a try.  This impressive set, at the time of purchase also had a $10 coupon , making this trail cam $69 and I was willing to give this is a try after reading some reviews and considering it was half of what we spent on our first one.  Right out of the box, this trail cam is aesthetically cool and very sturdy, the camo makes it great for hiding on most of our trails.  Very impressed with the fact that it comes with the 32gb card and card reader.  I feel like what's most impressive about this trail cam is the quality video, not only is it extremely clear and detailed, but the sound and visual 4K is just beautiful.  The resolution is quite impressive, and definitely blows our first one out of the water on most aspects.  Motion detection is also extremely impressive.  Keep in mind, all of these features are subject to placement, so just know that you will need stable, line of sight.  In other words your quality of sound and video, along with performance is only going to be as good as your choice of placement.  I had a friend that wasn't particularly aware of height when placing their trail camera outside their back door and she didn't place it high enough and a racoon easily got it and destroyed it, so always be mindful of that.  You really can't go wrong with this little trail cam and again for the price, it's absolutely worth it.  This would make a great gift for any outdoors person as well.  I hope this review is helpful!

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu I quite like this bottle.  I bought this in the 16 oz size and i maybe should have gone larger, as i really like the design.  I use this one for coffee, though If it were larger i would keep water in it.  The thing I like about this over others in the Kleen Kanteen range is the lip and threading.  The classic bottles have threading on the outside of the lip of the bottle with a cap which screws over the lip, clamping its edge against a gasket.  I have come to find this design prone to leaks if the gasket isn't properly seated.  The TKWide range just doesn't have this problem.  The threading is on the inside, low, under the lip of the bottle and the cap screws into it with a simple o ring.  I'm not a huge fan of the "cafe cap" but i just remove it and drink from the lip of the bottle which is itself quite comfortable.  It's kleer that kleen kanteen designed this bottle to work in exactly this way, as the lip of the bottle is the most comfortable of any i've ever encountered to drink from and they even make an assortment of different caps for this line with different features.  I'm considering getting the simple steel loop or bamboo cap to eliminate all remaining unnecessary parts.  The user experience drinking from the bottle with cap removed is similar to drinking from a tall glass tumbler.  The threading is recessed from the lip and doesn't interfere with drinking at all.. I also like that the 'cafe cap' is easily disassembled.. I hate cleaning these things, once a few weeks of coffee residue gets on them.  I've dropped this bottle twice and it has a dent now, but nothing severe.  I find it well made and well engineered and though, in my head at least, this bottle rivals the yeti ramblers which are similar, its about half of the price or less.
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu

GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing I selected this luminous key ring as an aid to attaching to my camera bag and being visible at night. I wasn’t exactly sure what to expect and I had some serious doubts about the effectiveness of this product. It turns out that it’s better than I had hoped and it works well.

The concept is very simple: expose it to bright light for a little while and it will glow in the dark for a longer while. The claim is that it will glow for up to 10 hours; I have not verified that it will last that long, but it does go for a long time, long enough in most situations that it will continue to glow long after sunset. This is really all I can ask.

The vial appears to be filled with some sort of phosphorous-coated granules. As a first test I exposed them to the bright light of an LED flashlight for about 30 seconds, and the vial glowed for several minutes afterward. It wasn’t all that bright, but I didn’t give it long to “charge” either. It was enough as a proof of concept though. It lasts longer under extended exposure to bright light such as direct sunlight.

The extra clips that come with the vial are useful for attaching it to other things without using the ring. One of the attachments is actually the same thing as a pen clip, which is useful for clipping to a tent flap, umbrella or other fabric surface.

Especially when considering the cost, this is really an easy product to recommend if you need a luminous marker. It really does work for a long while, it’s very easy to see and it is versatile.
text_fidelity_b: GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing

text_fidelity_a:
MIAODAM Exercise Wheel and Resistance Band Ordered these for my son who’s struggled through quarantine to get an appropriate work out.. I know, I know- we’re all singing the same sad quarantine song (some in better tune than others-ha-ah!) This was an all inclusive workout set sold at a decent price point and although we had high hopes it would be as great as our gym membership.. (yeah, right!! We all need realistic expectations ..) this had its perks and drawback- ultimately, I would have liked to rate it 3.5 star. I would suggest this is set mean for beginners/novice level exercise enthusiast.. and could meet those needs fairly well. (Used 2-3x week and for 15-30min. at a time..) However, this might fall short for those expecting a little more from their equipment..

If purchasing keep in mind:

-The grip handles are smaller than some adult male hands..(at least in our house!) Obviously, this could prove problematic if.. ones grip is compromised right from the start. However, an adult females hand seems to fit the grip without issue.

-As with any elastic band the stretch is tighter when you begin. This set offers varied resistance (clearly marked by color) after x30 day use.. Lower resistance bands are showing more signs of “slack.” (Nothing has snapped on us! But, the lesser band is much easier to pull.. and I would beg to differ it’s because we’re getting so much stronger!!) Higher levels still have plenty of resistance but, we haven’t used nearly as much so, they stretch out - just something to keep in mind.

-Protect door jam with extra padding!! As these are braced against “wood” with a soft rounded ball, we have found- not all door jams are created equal (i’m pretty sure our door jams are made of wood composite?!!) So, be careful and add a small cut out of foam, washcloth or dish towel.. Anything you can easily rig to buffer The wall and protect it- bc, we noticed small indents being left on the door jam itself- not what we wanted and overtime without protection… It’ll only get worse!

-Appreciate the bag this came with to store all the items in along with the extra straps/gadgets. This does have instructions- however, they’re a bit tricky to read- just know you can Google a “how to video“ and obtain the info. easily enough . Would have loved to see this set contain added buffer pad for walls.. even a few photos with instructions- possibly something included in the future? I’d also appreciate including a magic eraser for the walls! The black rubber can leave small markings… Yes! These easily come off with wall eraser- Hence, the perk of including one in the bag!

Overall, this is not a bad set up. It can give a person- a good resistance workout.. It just has a few idiosyncrasies to work around.. I suggest knowing your audience and their physical size and ability… If, you do prior to any ordering- and are sure to protect the physical structure of the door when setting up- then, one should get what you need from this workout set.

I hope this info helps… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: MIAODAM Exercise Wheel and Resistance Band

text_fidelity_a: Tulov Double Camping Sleeping Pad, Self Inflating Camping Pad, Waterproof Foot Pump Air Mattresses Portable Sleeping Mat for 2 Person Hiking Traveling Backpacking I've used this pad a few times now and every time I've been disappointed.  Sleeping after a long day backpacking is always welcomed.  I wanted to see how well this mat would perform but so far I've yet to have a good experience with it.  In most cases, it will lose air.  Nothing has punctured the pad and I see no air leaks if I attempt to do bubble tests and whatnot on it but for some reason I inevitably will end up waking up on the ground.  Even when it is fully inflated, it's not the most comfortable pad.  The hexagons sound like a great idea but the reality is if you're kneeling on it or have an elbow on it, odds are you're going to kneel or rest your elbow on the ground in the gaps between the hexagons.  Filling it with air is no different than any of the other pads of this style.  Takes time but great that you do not need to carry around anything extra.  It's heavy, so if you're an ultralight backpacker, there are lighter alternatives out there.  Wish I could give this a better review but I've since switched to one of my other pads that is far more comfortable.

Exped MegaMat 10 Duo | Self-Inflating Camping Mat for Two | Extremely Comfortable & Luxurious Sleeping Pad, Green, Long Wide Plus I'm an avid camper and outdoors person. I recently decided it was time for an upgrade from using my parent's 1980's foam mats that have been awkwardly combined with my partner's giant trifold (and not waterproof) cushion. We camp frequently near our truck and will have a Go Fast roof top camper added in the coming months which we intend to use this in.

Here's my take - The mat is extremely durable!!! WAY more so than the air mattresses we've used before that require an electric pump. My large dogs walked across the mat several times and no marks were left. I'm not worried at all about tears or punctures with this material, and am happy to see it's rated for cold weather.
We laid three adults across it and it was comfortable but snug, so it's definitely comfortable enough for two with room to spare. The mat feels more like a memory foam topper with just the right amount of give for your hips and shoulders if you are a side sleeper. I found it comfortable to lay on my back and stomach too.

It comes with a mini foot pump attachment which easily helped us get it fully inflated (we waited about an hour or so and it self-inflated about an inch, then we got impatient and finished inflating in about 5 minutes). The valves are well-made and appear very durable. It also comes with a carry case for storage and travel.

I would definitely NOT want to lug this thing into the woods for a backpacking venture due to its size. But for car camping or tent camping close to your vehicle I absolutely recommend! The steep price tag is the only downside I can think of.
text_fidelity_b: Exped MegaMat 10 Duo | Self-Inflating Camping Mat for Two | Extremely Comfortable & Luxurious Sleeping Pad, Green, Long Wide Plus

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver Easy to setup and adjust, feels sturdy and secure. It really would take a bit of effort to remove a bike from it if you have it locked down.

Seems like a really good value.

There were a few stumbling blocks I encountered, though. First, the locking hitch pin that Sawgman sells is a bit expensive, compared to other locking pins you can find. However, because the rack had a threaded hole, a standard 1/2” pin won’t fit through. I ended up just yawing the supplied pin, and used a small Master Lock with a small enough shackle diameter to fit. Probably not as secure as the proprietary locking pin, but it should be enough to dissuade anyone looking for a quick grab and go.

Speaking of shackle diameter, it was a bit of a challenge to find the perfect locks to use on the bars. Your typical MasterLock is about 7mm, which is too big; and 5mm was small enough that you could still pull the trigger and move the bar up with ease. In the end I found the MasterLock 141T set of two locks (Keyed alike) with a 6mm shackle was the best fit. The shackle is just small enough to fit through the hole, but thick enough to keep the trigger secure.

So the TLDR, but a lock with a 6mm diameter shackle to secure your bikes.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver

text_fidelity_a:
Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster I wanted to try a drop leg holster for some time and came across this model in desert camo through another vendor. For the price, and because I had heard good things about Fox, I decided to take advantage of the reduced price and see how good (or bad) this holster really is.

The first day, after strapping it on and making all the adjustments I could, I carried around a mini ball peen hammer just to try to get used to it. Why did I choose a hammer? While I am CCW licensed, Florida does not currently allow "open carry". So I had to put something of measurable weight in the holster without alarming the neighbors or anyone driving by on our street. I could imagine someone seeing me with a drop leg holster and calling our local law enforcement, not knowing that their was no gun in the holster -- but assuming there was.Yes, the weight of the hammer head made the holster cant backwards, so I switched to a rubber mallet. This provided a much better balance.

Then I switched to a Glock 23 and a Springfield XD-45 MOD 2 and alternately carried both around inside our home, After trying my darndest to get it to fit properly, I came to the following conclusions:

1. This is a cool looking and well constructed rig. The desert camo design is well done, the material is light and flexible, and the various
clips, belts and fasteners work like they should.
2 The holster accommodated both the Springfield and Glock perfectly and the strap easily fastened over the gun butt.
3. It is very light and designed to fit comfortably against your thigh.
4. And of course it easily carries a lighter weight weapon like a Kahr PM9 and a Glock 42. In fact the smaller and lighter pistols eliminate
the bounding around explained below. But who wants to carry a "pocket pistol" in a drop leg holster?

But, and this is a "big but" for me, the single strap that fastens the holster around your thigh just couldn't keep the holster secure and steady. It bounced while walking and really moved around when running (even at my slow pace). I tightened the thigh strap so that over 14" of strap was outside the buckle, but it just never felt secure. No one wants that feeling -- you want your gun to be right where it's supposed to be -- all of the time.

This holster really needs two improvements: 1. It needs a second strap to go around the thigh, one high and one low. 2. It also needs more vertical adjustment so that it can be carried a bit higher on your belt. Both of these changes would result in a better fit and should eliminate excess movement.
text_fidelity_b: Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster

Carbon Tactics Quicky - Magnetic Tactical Belt (Regular) I quite liked the idea of the Carbon Tactics Quicky. A superstrong belt that could double as a strap, plus a cool buckle? Count me in.

First off, the buckle is very well-thought out and designed. I found myself playing with it, because it’s fun to open and close. All you have to do is press down and twist to open, while closing is even easier, thanks to the magnets. This could be helpful if you have trouble with regular belts. I haven’t ever had it accidentally open.

The nylon of the belt strap feels very heavy duty and secure; my mom actually used the belt for therapy, to help stretch her legs. She worried that lighter weight straps would break or slip free from her grasp, but she didn’t have that fear with the Quicky belt.

However, when I tried to use the Quicky *as* a belt, I ran into some problems. I wear a 30” waist in jeans, so at 50” long, the Quicky belt was very long for me. There’s an elastic loop to secure extra length, but if you pull in as much of the belt as I did, there was an unsightly/unsafe gap between my waist and the excess length. I *could* cut the belt strap to make it shorter and get rid of that unsafe gap, but then I would be limiting myself on other uses for the belt. While the inventor did a good job with other aspects of the belt, I wish he had considered other options for when the belt is used on a smaller waist.
text_fidelity_b: Carbon Tactics Quicky - Magnetic Tactical Belt (Regular)

Rubbermaid Victory Jug, 2 Gallon, Modern Red FG153004MODRD We debated whether to buy this water jug or another, more sturdy jug by another manufacturer for more than twice the money. We decided to buy the other jug when we found the Rubbermaid on sale at a local store for less than 1/3rd the cost of the more sturdy jug. For the difference in price we thought we'd give the Rubbermaid a try to see how it would perform.

The lower spigot on the Rubbermaid is solid. No leaks and easy to use. The upper vent spigot is a little bit of a weak point. It works absolutely fine, just remember to always close it so it doesn't get broken or let hot air cycle into the cold interior of the jug.

Although not an "extreme" cooler jug, once filled with ice and water we had cold water well into the second day in the desert. The cooler was kept in the shade the entire time.

If you need a rough and tumble water jug, look elsewhere. If you need something that will sit on a picnic table for a day or two, this will work fine.

Hydration Belt for Running - Includes Accessories and Two 10-Ounce BPA-Free and Leak-Proof Water Bottles : A Bounce-Free & Lightweight Fuel Gear While hydration packs are very useful to have, they tend to look more like medical support equipment or, at best, just plain geeky. This one, however, dials the geek factor way down. Not completely, but it's well done.

The build quality is excellent. The belt itself is neoprene that is well-stitched and assembled. It feels very solid and able to withstand more than an ample amount of punishment. The waist straps are elastic which is far better than the usual web material since it stretches easily to maintain its position in use without rubbing your skin raw from bouncing around. The elastic is also covered with a sort of felt-type material. Both the straps and the belt itself are very comfortable to wear -- zero problems with movement.

The bottles fit into neoprene holsters that hold them firmly. I had zero issues with the bottles coming out when using this, but still had no problems taking the bottles out when I needed a drink. Getting them back into the holsters took a little more effort, but with some practice it became a one-handed operation. The bottles are square-ish in shape to keep them from sticking out too much when you're wearing the belt.

The front of the belt has a small pocket to stash a phone (or anything else). It has a zipper opening that operates easily and smoothly. I would have liked to see a somewhat larger zipper pull tab, but the current system works well.

The bottles are very soft - I'm going to guess they are made of HDPE since they are so easy to squeeze. They stand upright without any problem when taken out of the holster, and have a wide fill top for easy under-the-faucet filling. They have a pull-top for use that is a bit stiff to pull out, but it does seal well when closed. You do need to be careful about squeezing the bottle too much when taking a drink since the water comes out so quickly that you'll make a mess. But, that also adds to the cooling, and once you get the squeeze level down it's not an issue.

Overall, this is a very nicely made belt. It doesn't fully eliminate the geek factor of a hydration pack, but it does dial it down to an acceptable level, and has a lot of nice design touches to make it comfortable and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Hydration Belt for Running - Includes Accessories and Two 10-Ounce BPA-Free and Leak-Proof Water Bottles : A Bounce-Free & Lightweight Fuel Gear
